ตามการคาดการณ์ของ TrendForce ระบุว่า Enterprise SSD จะกลายเป็นเซกเมนต์การใช้งาน NAND Flash ที่ใหญ่ที่สุดในปี 2569 โดยคาดว่าราคาล่วงหน้าของ Client SSD จะเพิ่มขึ้นอย่างน้อย 40% ซึ่งถือเป็นการเพิ่มขึ้นที่มากที่สุดในบรรดาหมวดหมู่ผลิตภัณฑ์ NAND ทั้งหมด

results.title: TurboQuant Changes the Economics of Local AI Inference - Medium
results.content:
Numerous independent implementations. At least five different platforms. Consistent results. Implementations are already expanding beyond text LLMs: a vLLM plugin (`turboquant-vllm`) has been validated on vision-language models (Molmo2-4B/8B), where visual tokens create significantly higher KV cache pressure than text alone. The community-driven validation, without any code from Google, is itself a trust indicator. The results come from practitioners with no commercial incentive to inflate [...] Google Research published a blog post in March 2026 promoting TurboQuant , an algorithm available on arXiv since April 2025 and scheduled for presentation at ICLR 2026 in April . TurboQuant compresses the KV cache to as low as 3 bits, achieving at least 6x memory reduction in benchmark evaluations. No retraining. Near-zero accuracy degradation. For enterprise architects evaluating local inference, this changes the math.

## Why Memory Is the Real Bottleneck [...] Local AI inference does not fail because of model quality. It fails because of memory. TurboQuant proves that this bottleneck was never fundamental. It was an engineering problem, and it now has a mathematically near-optimal solution.

Near-zero accuracy loss at 6x KV cache compression. No training required. Independently validated by numerous community reimplementations on at least five different platforms, working from the paper alone, without any code from Google.

results.title: Will Google's TurboQuant technology save us? : r/StableDiffusion
results.content:
For TurboQuant to matter to someone, they'd have to be using one of those particular models, the KV cache memory use for it would have to be big enough to be worth optimizing, they'd have to accept the quality decrease that comes from quantizing the KV cache, and they'd also have to choose TurboQuant as the way to quantize it (and from what I've heard, it's not even as good as existing methods like Q4_0 with rotation). That's a lot of things that would have to align to make it relevant for a [...] It won't. First, people don't seem to understand the technology. TurboQuant does not reduce overall memory usage, it reduces the KV cache, which typically is a fraction of overall memory used by a model. Next, I am not sure why people go hype over models saving memory, when the additional efficiency will very likely be used for making better models, namely a larger context window.
